title: CI3 Sessions Part 2 — Check, Remove, Flash
description: Beyond load/set/use/destroy: checking a key exists, removing just one, and one-time flashdata messages.
congratsText: You handled the rest of the session toolkit!
objectives: Test whether a key exists with has_userdata before printing it
Remove a single key with unset_userdata instead of destroying everything
Store a one-time message with set_flashdata and read it with flashdata
Choose the right call for a given job
recap: has_userdata('key') returns TRUE or FALSE, so NULL never reaches the page.
unset_userdata('key') drops one key; sess_destroy() drops them all.
set_flashdata('key', value) lasts for the next request only, then CI3 clears it.
Lasting value: set_userdata. One-time notice: set_flashdata. Sign out: sess_destroy.

chunks.text: Last time userdata('username') gave NULL when nothing was stored. Printing NULL on a page looks broken to a visitor.

check.question: What does an unused key give back?

chunks.text: $this->session->has_userdata('username') answers yes or no instead. It returns TRUE or FALSE, never the value.
So a page can decide: if ($this->session->has_userdata('username')) show the name, otherwise send them to login().

check.question: Why check before you print?
options: So NULL never reaches the page
So the session loads much faster

quiz.question: What do the two var_dump lines print, in order?
options: maria and then NULL, since has_userdata returns the stored value
TRUE and then FALSE, since only one of the keys was ever set
TRUE and then TRUE, because the session box itself exists
FALSE and then FALSE, because has_userdata needs two arguments

chunks.text: $this->session->sess_destroy(); empties the whole box. Sometimes you only want one key gone.
$this->session->unset_userdata('username'); removes that one key. Every other key stays exactly where it was.

check.question: Does unset_userdata touch the other keys?

chunks.text: It is the same idea as PHP's own unset($_SESSION['username']), because that global is the session box.

check.question: Why does unset on $_SESSION do the same job?
options: It is the very same box
It is a backup of the box

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens into a logout() that keeps 'theme' but drops the login.

chunks.text: A 'Saved!' message should appear once. With set_userdata it would sit there on every page load afterwards.

check.question: What is wrong with a normal key here?

chunks.text: $this->session->set_flashdata('msg', 'Saved!'); stores it for the next request only. CI3 clears it after that on its own.
You read it the same way: $this->session->flashdata('msg'). Refresh a second time and it is NULL.

check.question: Refresh twice. What is in msg?

quiz.question: Type what the var_dump prints on the second refresh.

chunks.text: Name that should last the whole visit? Plain set_userdata. One-time notice? set_flashdata.

check.question: Which one for a 'Profile updated' notice?

chunks.text: Signing out for good? sess_destroy. Dropping a single key and keeping the rest? unset_userdata.

check.question: Which one keeps the other keys?

chunks.text: And before you print anything a visitor might not have, ask has_userdata first.

quiz.question: On the very next request, what is still readable?
options: Both theme and msg, since neither call removed anything yet
theme only, because unset_userdata just marks it for later
msg only, because flashdata survives exactly one more request
Neither one, because unset_userdata empties the whole box out
